analysis.title: Gold benefits from the US midterm election outcome
key_insights: Gold rebounded above USD 4,000/oz after the US midterm elections, helped by lower oil prices, a weaker USD and falling bond yields. Gold was among the few assets to benefit substantially from the outcome after heavy downward pressure ahead of the vote.

Before the election, risks looked skewed toward Middle East escalation and higher oil, alongside a firm USD and investor positioning for further dollar strength. Gold's inverse relationship with the USD has stayed strong, particularly since gold began retreating earlier this year.

UBS expects US political gridlock after the Democratic 'Blue wave' win of Congress, increased state-level AI regulation and weaker incentives for geopolitical escalation to keep modest downward pressure on the USD, supporting gold.

Markets appear to be pricing limited upside for oil and growing scope for normalization of energy supply and prices. Faster normalization would reinforce UBS's 2027 disinflation outlook and the view that major central banks, particularly the Fed, finish raising rates in 1Q.

UBS expects inflation to moderate more meaningfully in 2Q 2027, including in the US. Expectations of lower bond yields and potentially lower policy rates should then gain traction and support gold. The shift from further hikes to a pause and possible cuts will take time to emerge in 2027.
World Gold Council 3Q data show resilient demand. Total demand including OTC was 1,369 tonnes, down 1% y/y. Year-to-date demand was 3,881 tonnes, broadly in line with the 2025 record.

Central bank purchases rose 42% y/y to 321 tonnes. ETF inflows of 211 tonnes lifted global holdings to a record 4,256 tonnes. These offset weaker bar and coin demand (-19% y/y to 268 tonnes) and jewelry demand (-17% to 313 tonnes).
Jewelry demand fell 22% in China and 20% in India y/y. Technology demand rose 3% y/y on AI-related electronics.
Supply: mine production rose 3% y/y to a 3Q record 1,071 tonnes, recycling fell 8%, and total supply was 1% lower y/y.

UBS says strong central bank buying supports gold around USD 4,000/oz and that any renewed decline below that level should be limited as demand kicks in. A further investment-led rally likely needs a broader shift in monetary policy.
UBS keeps its view that gold rises in 2027 with a forecast of USD 5,000/oz or higher. It favors long gold exposure, and alternatively selling downside price risk to enhance yield.

tension_points.bull_case: Gridlock, a weaker USD, lower oil and falling yields support gold. Central bank buying of 321 tonnes and record ETF holdings underpin the USD 4,000/oz area, and disinflation in 2027 should bring a Fed pause and cuts.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran conflict hopes could recede, pushing oil higher and the USD firmer. Bar, coin and jewelry demand is weakening, and a further investment-led rally needs a broader monetary policy shift that will take time.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed decline below USD 4,000/oz that central bank demand fails to absorb.
